name: ManyChat
tagline: The comment-to-DM automation king for Instagram and WhatsApp, now charging by the active contact.
tldr: ManyChat is a chat marketing and automation platform built around Instagram, Facebook Messenger, and WhatsApp — best known for comment-to-DM automation that turns social engagement directly into conversations.

Pricing was overhauled in March 2026 to scale by active monthly contacts across four tiers: Free (25 contacts, 2 channels), Essential ($17/mo, 250 contacts), Pro ($39/mo, 2,500 contacts, AI included), and Business ($69/mo, 7,500 contacts), plus per-contact overage fees once you exceed plan limits.
Founded in 2015, headquartered in the US (San Francisco/West Hollywood), and backed by roughly $158M in venture funding across three rounds, led by CEO and co-founder Mikael Yang.

Reviews are strong on core automation and flow-building (G2 and Capterra both trend well above 4/5), but Reddit and Trustpilot threads consistently cite cost escalation as contact lists grow, slow support, and occasional flow/automation reliability glitches.

The March 2026 pricing overhaul cut the free tier from 1,000 contacts down to just 25, a change that drew significant user pushback and is worth flagging to anyone comparing ManyChat's free tier against competitors.
keyFeatures: Comment-to-DM automation that triggers a direct message flow whenever someone comments on an Instagram post, reel, or ad
Visual flow builder for multi-step automated conversations across Instagram, Messenger, and WhatsApp without code
AI-included automation on the Pro tier and above for smarter reply handling within built flows
Contact tagging and segmentation for targeted broadcast campaigns and re-engagement of past leads
Template library for duplicating proven automation flows in minutes rather than building from scratch
Native integrations plus Zapier connectivity for linking flows to external CRMs and tools
Growth tools (Instagram Story mentions, keyword triggers, QR codes) designed specifically for social-commerce lead capture
Per-contact overage billing that scales cost directly with active monthly contact volume rather than a flat seat fee

companyInfo.hq: San Francisco / West Hollywood, California, US

faq.question: How does ManyChat's pricing work in 2026?
faq.answer: As of the March 2026 pricing overhaul, plans scale by active monthly contacts: Free (25 contacts, 2 channels), Essential ($17/mo for 250 contacts), Pro ($39/mo for 2,500 contacts, includes AI), and Business ($69/mo for 7,500 contacts). Exceeding your contact limit triggers per-contact overage fees that decrease in rate at higher tiers.

faq.question: What happened to ManyChat's free plan?
faq.answer: The free tier was cut from 1,000 contacts down to 25 contacts as part of the March 2026 pricing restructure — a roughly 97.5% reduction that drew significant user criticism, since it makes the free plan effectively a trial rather than a usable small-business tier.

faq.question: What is ManyChat best known for?
faq.answer: Comment-to-DM automation on Instagram — automatically messaging anyone who comments on a post, reel, or ad — is consistently the most-praised, standout feature in independent reviews, used heavily for lead capture and engagement growth.

faq.question: Does ManyChat support WhatsApp?
faq.answer: Yes, WhatsApp is one of the core supported channels alongside Instagram and Facebook Messenger, though WhatsApp-specific messaging fees from Meta apply on top of ManyChat's own plan pricing.

faq.question: What do users complain about most?
faq.answer: Cost escalation as contact lists grow is the most repeated Reddit complaint, with some users reporting bills growing 2-3x as their lists expanded. Slow, email-only support and occasional automation reliability glitches (flows failing to fire, profiles disconnecting mid-campaign) are the other recurring themes.

scorecard.note: Reviewers consistently describe building Instagram/Messenger/WhatsApp flows without technical skill, often duplicating templates in under five minutes.
AI is included from the Pro tier up, but is generally seen as a add-on to flow automation rather than a standout conversational AI compared to dedicated AI-support platforms.
Strong on Instagram, Messenger, and WhatsApp specifically, but lacks the broader email/voice/ticketing coverage of helpdesk-style competitors.
The March 2026 shift to per-contact pricing with a 25-contact free tier and steep overage fees is the most consistently criticized aspect of the product in recent reviews.
G2 reviewers score functionality well but flag customer service as a comparative weak point, with Reddit threads describing slow, email-only support especially on billing issues.

pros: Comment-to-DM automation on Instagram is a genuinely differentiated, well-reviewed feature for social-led lead generation
Visual flow builder is approachable enough for non-technical marketers to build and duplicate working automations quickly
Well-funded, established player (founded 2015, ~$158M raised) with a large existing template and integration ecosystem
AI included starting at a relatively affordable Pro tier ($39/mo) compared to some AI-first competitors' enterprise-gated AI
cons: March 2026 pricing overhaul slashed the free tier from 1,000 to just 25 contacts, drawing significant user backlash
Per-contact overage billing makes costs escalate quickly and unpredictably as a business's audience grows
Support is frequently described as slow and email-only, particularly frustrating during billing disputes
Coverage is concentrated on Instagram/Messenger/WhatsApp — no native email helpdesk, ticketing, or voice channel

sentiment.quote: The automation allowed me to connect with customers without having to be tied to my phone responding to messages.
I must admit that it is the market leader for the chatbot sector, I find it a very useful tool for creating interesting workflows.
The pricing is too high, and integrating with other tools required lots of patchwork zapier solutions.

bestFor: Social-first brands driving leads and sales through Instagram comments, DMs, and Stories
E-commerce and D2C businesses wanting WhatsApp and Messenger automation for conversational commerce
Marketers who want a visual, no-code flow builder over a more traditional support-ticket interface
Small teams whose contact list will stay within a predictable range, avoiding overage-fee surprises
verdict: ManyChat still owns comment-to-DM automation on Instagram better than anyone else in this list, and the flow builder genuinely lets a non-technical marketer ship a working funnel in an afternoon. But the March 2026 move to per-contact pricing — gutting the free tier from 1,000 contacts to 25 — is a real shift in who this product is for, and the Reddit threads about bills growing 2-3x as a list scales aren't exaggerating the mechanics of the new model. Great fit for a brand that lives on Instagram and WhatsApp and keeps its contact list lean; a riskier bet for anyone expecting the free-tier generosity ManyChat used to be known for.
